status: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. Expected outcomes fixed here; no row may be dropped or re-scoped after results.

authorisation.allowed: construct and execute counterexamples ONLY inside isolated copies of the real StrictOnlineEnv, recording actual before/after state differences
authorisation.stop_condition: every pre-registered counterexample reaches a definite, re-checkable conclusion, then STOP

critical_reporting_rule: F10 is EXPECTED to reproduce the bypass. A successfully reproduced defect must be recorded as COUNTEREXAMPLE_REPRODUCED and must NOT be reported as 'G-L passes'. Reproducing a defect is not fixing it and not certifying it.

counterexamples.name: a path that executes an illegal suffix with NO composed certification
counterexamples.construction: on an isolated copy: set every vehicle needs_replan=False so the replanner is never invoked, write an ILLEGAL suffix (containing an already-served customer) directly into v.mutable_suffix exactly as a replanner would, then run the env's OWN commit loop (StrictOnlineEnv._plan_and_commit) with no gate and no certifier in the loop
counterexamples.expected: the illegal head IS committed; before/after state diff shows committed_next/status changed
counterexamples.must_not: be reported as G-L passing; be papered over by calling the composed gate inside the test
counterexamples.assertion: committed_next == the served customer AND the composed certifier was never called in this path

counterexamples.name: TOCTOU: state changes between certification and the FIRST real write
counterexamples.construction: stage 1: pre_install_reverify on matching credentials at state version S1 -> allow=True. stage 2: change the state on the copy (clear a mutable tail and/or advance the clock) -> S2. stage 3: call the real write primitive (_commit) with the S1-approved plan, WITHOUT re-checking
counterexamples.expected: the write proceeds; the approval and the write are separated by an uncontrolled interval, so a hash re-comparison alone does not make the commit atomic
counterexamples.must_not: claim atomicity from the existence of the identity comparison; implement a new production commit path
counterexamples.assertion: allow was True at S1, the state changed to S2, and _commit still wrote (committed_next changed) with no re-verification

counterexamples.name: does a later reveal / replanning invalidate the OLD credential on the real path
counterexamples.construction: across a real isolated run, capture credentials at consecutive decision points; identify a reveal event (visible-set growth); then pre_install_reverify(cred_k, cred_k+1)
counterexamples.expected: the identity components change and the comparison REFUSES
counterexamples.must_not: be upgraded to 'continuous safety holds', because no production path CALLS this comparison
counterexamples.assertion: state_hash (and/or plan_digest_anchor_v1) differs across the reveal AND pre_install_reverify refuses with an identity reason

counterexamples.name: _validate_state does not raise on a thermal excursion
counterexamples.construction: build a VehicleColdChainState whose compartment temperature is outside hard_temperature_bounds_c and pass it through transition_segment / _validate_state
counterexamples.expected: _validate_state does NOT raise; the excursion is only COUNTED by _thermal_violations
counterexamples.verdict_if_expected: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REPRODUCED (excursion tolerated, refused only post hoc)
counterexamples.assertion: no exception is raised while the violation counter increases

counterexamples.name: can the zone capacity floor bind
counterexamples.construction: analytic: for every zone, compare the temperature floor implied by the real loads (zone_load / thermal_capacity) against hard_upper - target
counterexamples.expected: report whether the floor can bind; a NO result is a definite conclusion
counterexamples.assertion: per-zone numbers reported with the explicit inequality

counterexamples.name: force _force_return_all and measure the physics-vs-delivery time gap
counterexamples.construction: on an isolated copy with a loaded 'ready' vehicle away from the depot, call env._force_return_all and compare the recorded return_arrival / delivered record time against the cold-chain advance time
counterexamples.expected: the recorded unload is EARLIER than the physics by the return travel time
counterexamples.verdict_if_expected: COUNTEREXAMPLE_REPRODUCED (recorded quality more optimistic than physics)
counterexamples.must_not: modify the historical physics; close the risk because the natural-run call count is zero
counterexamples.assertion: recorded delivery time < physics-derived delivery time by ~ the return travel time

point_1_quantifier_restriction.accepted: my strengthened claim ('tw_end[0]-now is the loosest sound duration bound, hard_upper the highest sound temperature, therefore the form can never bind') must NOT be generalised without limit: a larger arbitrary constant would formally lower the bound further while being meaningless. The correct statement is scoped to the contract's natural physical range and the whole-window bound.
point_1_quantifier_restriction.also_accepted: the ratio conclusion does NOT automatically cover every already-loaded lot: their Q_start is the CURRENT remaining quality, which need not equal the initial quality, so a lot already near the threshold could have a static bound below it even with a short remaining time.
point_1_quantifier_restriction.therefore: the valid claim is 'in this configuration, with initial quality 1, the static whole-window bound lacks refusal capability' -- NOT 'the static bound is non-discriminating for all states and lots'.

point_2_unique_writer.accepted: the unique writer must be 'a commit transaction AUTHORISED by the gate', NOT the gate becoming another VehicleState writer. Two write mechanisms (_plan_and_commit/_commit plus a new D3 install callback) would create a NEW bypass while nominally adding a gate.
point_2_unique_writer.required_architecture: keep exactly ONE real commit primitive and require every D3 target path to hold a currently valid credential BEFORE entering it
point_2_unique_writer.also_accepted: F8 cannot be discharged by re-comparing three hashes: it must guarantee that between the identity re-check and the first real state write there is no uncontrolled state change and no other writer

point_3_D0_ambiguity.accepted: D0's 'do not commit / preserve state' and the env's WAIT (mutable_suffix=[]) are NOT necessarily equivalent: clearing a non-empty mutable suffix IS itself a state change and may affect commitment fulfilment
required_split: REFUSE_NO_MUTATION: refuse the candidate and do not modify vehicle state
WAIT_BY_ENV_PROTOCOL: the original strict-online env legitimately produces WAIT, with an independent proof it does not violate accepted commitments
point_3_D0_ambiguity.rule: before formal acceptance these two must NOT both be described as 'zero state change'
